items.topic: Display behavior for the options block
items.context: The item description explicitly poses 'either always or behind a --full flag'. This is the central operator-experience decision. The human-first CLI principle from skill-principles favors showing useful info by default; flag-gating shifts cost from every decision-show invocation to operators who didn't know to ask.

options.label: Always show options when present (no flag)
options.rationale: Matches human-first CLI principle. Solves the original friction: operator never has to re-run with --json just to see option keys. Decisions without options pay zero cost (section is omitted). Recommended.

options.label: Show only behind a new --full (or --options) flag
options.rationale: Keeps default output compact. Costs an extra invocation and prior knowledge of the flag — re-introduces the exact friction this fix exists to solve, just with a different incantation than --json.

options.label: Show by default, but allow --compact to suppress
options.rationale: Best of both: default is operator-friendly, power users with scripted workflows can opt out. Adds one new flag.

items.context: Once we render options, how should each one look? Trade-off is scannability for operators choosing a key vs. terminal width for long labels/rationale.

options.label: Indented list: key + label on one line, rationale indented below; (recommended) marker after label when set
options.rationale: Matches the example in the plan's Target End State. Keys are easy to scan vertically. Rationale stays readable on narrow terminals. Recommended.

options.label: Aligned table (key | label | recommended | rationale)
options.rationale: Compact and grep-friendly, but rationale text often wraps and breaks columns; struggles in 80-col terminals.

options.label: One-line-per-option (key, label, recommended marker only; omit rationale unless --full)
options.rationale: Most compact; operator picks key fast but loses the workshop agent's per-option rationale unless they re-invoke.

items.context: The parent initiative states 'All work must ship across API + CLI + UI per the operator's three-surface parity rule.' This particular item, however, is framed as a CLI-only display gap — the API already returns options (--json shows them), so the API surface may already be correct. The UI may or may not render the options block in its decision-detail view. Resolving this scoping question early prevents either over-scoping (touching API needlessly) or under-scoping (shipping a CLI-only fix when the UI has the same gap).

options.label: CLI-only: API already returns options, assume UI renders them; verify quickly and ship CLI fix
options.rationale: Smallest, fastest fix. Aligns with the item's XS effort estimate. Recommended IF a quick UI spot-check confirms options are visible in the web UI's decision-detail view.

options.label: CLI + UI: extend scope if UI's decision-detail view also hides options or recommended flag
options.rationale: Honors the strict parity rule. Adds UI work to scope; bumps effort from XS toward S. Right call if UI is also broken.

options.label: Full three-surface audit: CLI + API + UI, even if API already exposes options
options.rationale: Most rigorous. Likely overkill since the bug surfaced is purely a CLI presentation gap; API was the workaround the operator already used.

items.text: Two recently-completed sibling items in this initiative (decision-deferral-primitive, decision-partial-accept-with-modifications) added new fields to the decision schema (deferred status, structured modifications). When implementing this fix, briefly confirm whether decision-show's human output also renders those fields, or whether their absence is a separate gap. If it's a gap, flag it for a new backlog item rather than expanding this fix's scope.

The prompt-manager source is not present in this workspace (this is the agent-manager repo with only a prompt-manager client). Executor will need to operate inside the prompt-manager scenario folder where the CLI command handler lives. This does not change the plan, but the executing agent should not waste cycles searching this repo for the formatter.

plan_updates: Created initial plan.md scaffold with all 13 mandatory sections populated. Problem statement and scope are fully specified from the rich item description. Implementation strategy is single-phase given XS effort. Three TBD areas captured as workshop decisions d1-d3 (display behavior, format/layout, three-surface parity scope). Risks include rationale-text wrapping, sibling-item parity, and potential API/UI scope creep.
